expression: ((sigma_peak*(1 + coupling_drift_scale*((E_cm/resonance_mass) - 1)*(1 + coupling_width_mix*intrinsic_width/resonance_mass)))*(resonance_mass**2*(intrinsic_width*(E_cm/resonance_mass)*(1 + width_relaxation_scale*((E_cm/resonance_mass)**2 - 1) + threshold_width_strength*sqrt(Piecewise((0, E_cm < channel_threshold_energy), (E_cm/channel_threshold_energy - 1, True)))))**2)/((E_cm**2 - resonance_mass**2)**2 + resonance_mass**2*(intrinsic_width*(E_cm/resonance_mass)*(1 + width_relaxation_scale*((E_cm/resonance_mass)**2 - 1) + threshold_width_strength*sqrt(Piecewise((0, E_cm < channel_threshold_energy), (E_cm/channel_threshold_energy - 1, True)))))**2))/(1 + beam_energy_spread**2/((intrinsic_width*(E_cm/resonance_mass)*(1 + width_relaxation_scale*((E_cm/resonance_mass)**2 - 1) + threshold_width_strength*sqrt(Piecewise((0, E_cm < channel_threshold_energy), (E_cm/channel_threshold_energy - 1, True)))))**2 + (E_cm - resonance_mass)**2))

new_symbol_range_suggestions.channel_threshold_energy: approximately within the scanned E_cm interval or within a few intrinsic_width of resonance_mass when the threshold effect is intended to be observable
new_symbol_range_suggestions.threshold_width_strength: nonnegative and typically small to order unity so the threshold-opened partial-width contribution is comparable to or smaller than the baseline smooth width variation across the scan

derivation_notes: The smooth off-shell width law is refined by allowing an additional decay mode to open only above a definite channel_threshold_energy, contributing a phase-space-like sqrt(E_cm/channel_threshold_energy - 1) term to the effective total width. This one-sided nonanalytic onset feeds into both the Breit-Wigner denominator and the beam-spread attenuation factor, producing a cusp-like shoulder distortion while reducing to the parent when the threshold contribution vanishes.
change_summary: I promoted the nearby decay-threshold location to a new independently sampled input and made the width coefficient depend on it through a one-sided square-root onset. This changes the target mapping sigma(E_cm) by creating asymmetric threshold-induced curvature that the parent's globally smooth width law cannot localize to one side of the resonance.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: The total width varies smoothly with energy across the whole scan and no nearby decay channel opens within the sampled region.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Threshold opening of an additional allowed decay mode modifies the total width with a kinematic cusp above its onset, feeding back into the resonant denominator and hence the measured cross section.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: The successor reduces to the parent in the limit threshold_width_strength -> 0; equivalently, when channel_threshold_energy lies far outside the scanned energies so the Piecewise threshold term remains inactive or negligible over the dataset.

response_change.parent_relation: The parent uses a smooth polynomial-like energy dependence of the effective width and coupling, so the line shape remains analytically rounded on both sides of the peak with no channel-opening kink.
response_change.child_relation: Relax the assumption that the total width varies smoothly across the whole scan by allowing a nearby decay-channel threshold to turn on phase space nonanalytically, adding a cusp-like contribution to the effective width above threshold while leaving the isolated-resonance structure intact.
response_change.observable_effect: When the scan crosses a kinematically nearby decay threshold, the measured cross section develops an asymmetric shoulder or sharper curvature change on one side of the peak that a single smooth parent width law cannot match simultaneously with the opposite side using one shared parameter set.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when a relevant decay-channel threshold lies within roughly a few intrinsic widths of the scanned region and beam_energy_spread is not so large that it smooths out the threshold-induced cusp; strongest when beam_energy_spread is comparable to or smaller than intrinsic_width.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, the mechanism appears as side-dependent curvature near the resonance shoulder; in holdout farther along the same scan, the same threshold-opening law continues to reshape the tail instead of remaining a globally smooth numerator/width drift.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent when the threshold lies far outside the scanned energies or when the threshold-coupled contribution tends to zero, so the effective width reduces to the existing smooth energy-dependent form.
evolution_contract.promotion_reason: A genuine threshold effect requires the independently set location of the relevant channel-opening energy; no existing symbol specifies where the nonanalytic onset occurs, so one new sampled input is needed to represent the external condition of which nearby threshold is kinematically relevant.
evolution_contract.domain_mechanism: threshold opening of an additional decay channel in the resonance total width
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Threshold opening of an additional allowed decay mode modifies the total width with a kinematic cusp above its onset, feeding back into the resonant denominator and hence the measured cross section.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because the width coefficient now changes regime at a sampled threshold location and introduces one-sided nonanalytic curvature tied to the relative ordering of E_cm and channel_threshold_energy, not a global rescaling or smooth retuning.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: The effective total width is globally smooth across the scan and no nearby channel-opening threshold affects the line shape.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: An additional decay mode opens at channel_threshold_energy and contributes a one-sided square-root phase-space term to the effective width above threshold.
evolution_contract.after_fragment: ((sigma_peak*(1 + coupling_drift_scale*((E_cm/resonance_mass) - 1)*(1 + coupling_width_mix*intrinsic_width/resonance_mass)))*(resonance_mass**2*(intrinsic_width*(E_cm/resonance_mass)*(1 + width_relaxation_scale*((E_cm/resonance_mass)**2 - 1) + threshold_width_strength*sqrt(Piecewise((0, E_cm < channel_threshold_energy), (E_cm/channel_threshold_energy - 1, True)))))**2)/((E_cm**2 - resonance_mass**2)**2 + resonance_mass**2*(intrinsic_width*(E_cm/resonance_mass)*(1 + width_relaxation_scale*((E_cm/resonance_mass)**2 - 1) + threshold_width_strength*sqrt(Piecewise((0, E_cm < channel_threshold_energy), (E_cm/channel_threshold_energy - 1, True)))))**2))/(1 + beam_energy_spread**2/((intrinsic_width*(E_cm/resonance_mass)*(1 + width_relaxation_scale*((E_cm/resonance_mass)**2 - 1) + threshold_width_strength*sqrt(Piecewise((0, E_cm < channel_threshold_energy), (E_cm/channel_threshold_energy - 1, True)))))**2 + (E_cm - resonance_mass)**2))
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: Take threshold_width_strength -> 0, or place channel_threshold_energy sufficiently far outside the scanned energies so the threshold term stays inactive or negligible, and the parent expression is recovered.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: At fixed resonance_mass, intrinsic_width, beam_energy_spread, and coupling parameters, varying E_cm across channel_threshold_energy produces a one-sided curvature change: below threshold the line shape follows the parent's smooth trend, while above threshold the effective width rises more abruptly and suppresses or broadens that shoulder. This is observable when the threshold lies within or near the scan and beam smearing does not erase the cusp.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set can only alter sigma(E_cm) through globally smooth reduced-energy drift in the numerator and width. Refitting all existing parent parameters may redistribute overall peak height, width, and smooth asymmetry, but it cannot create a localized onset tied to the sampled channel_threshold_energy that leaves the opposite side governed by the original smooth law. Separate fits for different threshold locations would evade the test, but one shared parent set ignoring the new input is structurally unable to reproduce the threshold-anchored shoulder distortion across those conditions.

evolution_plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, the mechanism appears as side-dependent curvature near the resonance shoulder; in holdout farther along the same scan, the same threshold-opening law continues to reshape the tail instead of remaining a globally smooth numerator/width drift.
evolution_plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent when the threshold lies far outside the scanned energies or when the threshold-coupled contribution tends to zero, so the effective width reduces to the existing smooth energy-dependent form.
evolution_plan.promotion_reason: A genuine threshold effect requires the independently set location of the relevant channel-opening energy; no existing symbol specifies where the nonanalytic onset occurs, so one new sampled input is needed to represent the external condition of which nearby threshold is kinematically relevant.
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes the off-shell width changes smoothly with energy, but a nearby decay channel can open at a specific energy and induce a nonanalytic phase-space onset in the total width, altering the observed line shape.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: The resonance mass, intrinsic width, and channel coupling are constant across the scan.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Threshold opening of an additional allowed decay mode modifies the total width with a kinematic cusp above its onset, feeding back into the resonant denominator and hence the measured cross section.
evolution_plan.rationale: Parent response relationship: varying E_cm at fixed resonance_mass, intrinsic_width, beam_energy_spread, and coupling parameters changes sigma through a single isolated resonance whose effective width and numerator drift smoothly with reduced energy. Scientific gap: real unstable states often sit near the opening of another decay channel, where phase space turns on only above a definite threshold and the total width is not globally smooth. Child response change: as E_cm crosses that threshold, the width acquires extra one-sided curvature, which lowers and broadens the affected shoulder of the resonance more abruptly than any smooth polynomial relaxation can. Distinguishing condition: compare scan points below and above a nearby threshold while holding the same shared resonance parameters fixed; the child predicts a kink-like asymmetry or shoulder-specific suppression, whereas the parent with one shared refitted parameter set can only redistribute smooth slope and curvature across the whole scan and cannot localize the change to one side without spoiling the opposite side. This is a changed target mapping, not merely an auxiliary reinterpretation, because sigma(E_cm) itself changes. Admissible conditions: the threshold must lie within or near the sampled energy interval and not be fully washed out by beam spread. Limitation: if the threshold is remote or beam smearing dominates, the refinement becomes practically unidentifiable and the parent is an adequate approximation.

selected_embedding_pattern.description: Make the coefficient of an existing process depend on a declared quantity.

scenario_text: An accelerator experiment scans the center-of-mass energy of two colliding particles near a single unstable intermediate state. The measured response is the total production cross section for a specified decay channel at each independently selected collision energy. The baseline model attributes the energy dependence to resonant production followed by decay with a constant intrinsic width. Detector smearing, nonresonant production, and interference are held fixed or neglected.
promotion_reason: A genuine threshold effect requires the independently set location of the relevant channel-opening energy; no existing symbol specifies where the nonanalytic onset occurs, so one new sampled input is needed to represent the external condition of which nearby threshold is kinematically relevant.
